attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, written after he quotes Hassabis. The forecast sentence is his, not a quotation.

semantics.note: 'We won't see AGI this decade' is a firm will_not forecast. The proposition keeps the horizon and treats 'not even close' and the cited reasons as supporting content, which is faithful.

contract.note: Reading 'this decade' as the 2020s ending 2029-12-31 is the ordinary reading. Using the AGI definition endorsed in context and a public-demonstration test is fair. The early-resolution rule only allows early contradiction, which is appropriate.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement (2026-10-26) of AI-produced discoveries. It is a company disclosure with no independent validation. It does not show one system meeting the full definition, including art and physical intelligence.
Google's own disclosure (2026-10-27) of progress in embodied reasoning. It covers physical intelligence only and does not meet the cross-domain definition.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with a deadline of 2029-12-31, after the 2026-10-28 evaluation date. Nothing in the packet shows a verified public system meeting the full endorsed AGI definition, so the early-contradiction rule is not met. Absence of AGI before the deadline cannot support the forecast. The claim stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus explicitly endorses ('100% with') a view Hassabis stated. The endorsement is Marcus's own, but the forecast it carries is Hassabis's hedged estimate.

semantics.note: Saying Marcus agrees with the conservative 5-to-10-year view is faithful. The view he endorses is an approximate 'I think' estimate, and the drafter set the modality to 'likely'. In context, the commitment mainly rejects arrival around 2030; it is not a firm two-sided arrival window.

contract.note: The contract turns the endorsement into a firm 2031–2036 arrival window. It would count no AGI by 2036 as a contradiction. Marcus contrasted the view with the ~2030 estimate and never committed to AGI arriving by 2036. The upper bound is evaluator-supplied, and the hedged estimate should not be scored.

evidence.note: DeepMind's own essay (2026-09-16) saying AGI is near. It is a company opinion, not a demonstration, and has no bearing on the window.
Google's disclosure (2026-10-27) of robotics progress. It covers one capability only and does not meet the full definition.

reviews.rationale: The endorsed content is a hedged, approximate estimate ('I think', which the drafter coded as 'likely'), so policy says it is not scored. The contract also adds an upper-bound commitment Marcus never made. Even if the claim were scorable, the window runs to 2036, and no evidence shows early arrival of AGI under the full definition.
